Co-correspondence analysis relates two community matrices observed at the same
sites. Rows are matched by position, not sorted by their labels. Inputs must
be finite, non-negative numeric data with positive row totals. Empty species
are removed; at least two non-empty species and two sites are required.
Cross-validation requires at least three sites.

## Algorithms and provenance

The package ports the Matlab routines of Cajo J. F. ter Braak and Andre P.
Schaffers. The predictive SIMPLS routine derives from the `pls` implementation
by Ron Wehrens and Bjorn-Helge Mevik, adapted for weighted, uncentred analysis.
The package retains its GPL-2 licence and original authorship credits.

Symmetric CoCA uses weighted co-inertia decomposition. Predictive CoCA offers
SIMPLS and the original eigen-based algorithm. These are distinct formulations;
validation does not assume all output components are interchangeable.

Default symmetric-method weights come from the response matrix. To make the
weighting symmetric when swapping communities, set `symmetric = TRUE`, or
supply the same positive row weights to both fits. Axis signs are arbitrary;
comparisons should use fitted values, eigenvalues, or sign-aligned subspaces.

## Validation

The test suite compares weighted transforms with explicit matrix algebra,
checks inertia decomposition, and compares SIMPLS coefficients with
`pls::simpls.fit(..., center = FALSE)`. Fixed small data preserve established
0.4-6 results for symmetric eigenvalues, SIMPLS fitted values, CV fit, and
permutation statistics. Their generation seed and provenance are recorded in
`tests/testthat/fixtures/README.md`.

No original Matlab executable or reference output was available for this
modernization; Matlab numerical equivalence has not been established.

## Corrected behavior

The eigen branch now computes every requested axis when the response matrix
is at least as wide as the predictor matrix. Cross-validation supports one
axis and reports variance from the full-data fit: `Xvar`/`Xtotvar` for the
predictor and `Yvar`/`Ytotvar` for the response. This fixes row-order-dependent
variance summaries and incorrect response-block reporting.

Scaling floors include the equality boundary. `scaling = FALSE` now leaves
symmetric plotting scores unscaled. Loadings extraction and summary printing
have regression tests. Consult NEWS for all intentional behavior changes.

`centre` in `crossval()` and `R0` in `vegan::permutest()` remain compatibility
arguments with no effect. Row weights used by permutation tests are those
already incorporated in the fitted model. LOO CV retains the established
weighting convention; redesigning that estimator is outside this release.

## References

- ter Braak, C. J. F. and Schaffers, A. P. (2004). Co-correspondence analysis:
  a new ordination method to relate two community compositions. *Ecology*,
  85, 834–846.
- ter Braak, C. J. F. and de Jong, S. (1998). The objective function of partial
  least squares regression. *Journal of Chemometrics*, 12, 41–54.
